cases.title: Clamp boundaries
cases.subtitle: A regression caught
cases.explanation: The generated boundary tests fail on the changed implementation. The authored repair reply identifies a code bug and keeps the failing assertions. The same tests pass with the fixture's ground-truth fix.
cases.bug: clamp() swaps lo/hi in max/min, so every in-range value returns hi
cases.diff:
diff --git a/calc.py b/calc.py
index 9f221a6..cfe4453 100644
--- a/calc.py
+++ b/calc.py
@@ -5,6 +5,13 @@ def add(a, b):
     return a + b
 
 
+def clamp(x, lo, hi):
+    """Clamp x into the closed interval [lo, hi]."""
+    if lo > hi:
+        raise ValueError("lo must be <= hi")
+    return max(hi, min(lo, x))
+
+
 def mean(values):
     if not values:
         raise ValueError("mean of empty sequence")
cases.plan:
Plan for calc.clamp:
1. Value inside [lo, hi] is returned unchanged.
2. Value below lo returns lo; value above hi returns hi.
3. Boundaries lo and hi are returned unchanged.
4. lo > hi raises ValueError.
cases.message: clamp(5, 0, 10) returns 10 and clamp(-3, 0, 10) returns 10: the expression `max(hi, min(lo, x))` has lo and hi swapped, so it always returns hi. The tests encode the documented contract ("clamp x into [lo, hi]"); the fix is `max(lo, min(hi, x))`.

cases.title: Even-length median
cases.subtitle: A regression missed
cases.explanation: The generated tests cover odd-length inputs and pass while the even-length bug remains. An independent authored boundary witness fails on that implementation and passes with the fixture's ground-truth fix.
cases.bug: median() returns the upper middle element for even-length input instead of the mean of the two middles
cases.diff:
diff --git a/stats.py b/stats.py
index 1031c7b..a851be6 100644
--- a/stats.py
+++ b/stats.py
@@ -3,3 +3,12 @@
 
 def total(values):
     return sum(values)
+
+
+def median(values):
+    """Median of a non-empty sequence (mean of the two middle values if even)."""
+    if not values:
+        raise ValueError("median of empty sequence")
+    s = sorted(values)
+    mid = len(s) // 2
+    return s[mid]
cases.plan:
Plan for stats.median:
1. Odd-length unsorted input.
2. Single element.
3. Empty input raises ValueError.
